top_concerns: The 1/sqrt(k) scaling is only meaningful for k < C*; for k >~ C* the filtered set contains y* and the problem is trivial, and the bound is vacuous when C* eps^2 >= k
Strong assumptions (unique y*, on-policy reward error, C* = 1/pi_ref(y*)) and the threshold alpha needs the unknown C*; experiments use hand-set alpha with no sensitivity analysis
The scaling-monotonicity definition does not imply performance never degrades with N, so the 'no degradation' claim is overstated; BoN's k-scaling is left unresolved
Experiments are thin and noisy (no error bars, AIME24 with 30 problems), with missing baselines such as weighted voting and sum/max-aggregated BoN
The theoretical novelty over Huang et al. 2025 is modest (pessimism filter plus Chernoff and Cauchy-Schwarz)
